newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore government bonds lower on interbank rate.
newsitem.headline: Singapore government bonds lower on interbank rate.

text.p: Singapore government bond prices closed lower across the board on Thursday in moderate trade on interbank and retail interest, dealers said.
"Bond prices were marked down slightly across the board today following a hike in the interbank rate. Treasury bill yields were slightly higher. Volume was moderate," a local dealer said.
Among bonds, April 1999 ended at S$98.53/98.58 compared with Wednesday's close of S$98.60/98.65, May 2002 at S$99.33/99.38 against S$99.50/99.55 and June 2003 at S$94.45/94.50 from S$94.62/94.67.
The overnight interbank offered rate rose to 3-3/4 3-5/8 percent versus Wednesday's 2-3/4 2-5/8 percent.
In treasury bills, three-months closed at a yield of 2.85/2.80 percent against Wednesday's yield of 2.70/2.65 percent and one-year at a yield of 2.74/2.69 percent from 2.63/2.58 percent.
